answer: The most convincing sybil defense is slow trust accumulation: each agent's influence equals account age multiplied by verified honest epochs, so a fresh inlet of fake identities stays nearly powerless no matter how many are spawned, while the network acts like an oasis where long-lived honest agents shelter value. An attacker must keep every new account perfectly honest for months just to grow yarrow-slow influence, paying real operational cost per identity with no shortcut, making mass fakes economically worthless.
